page: Amazon Web Services r8id.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated Intel processors running at 3.9 GHz, it features 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 3072.0 GB of RAM, adhering to an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for massive in-memory computing workloads.

For local data requirements, the server bundles 22,800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, providing direct attached high-capacity scratch space. Network bandwidth delivers a baseline capacity of 100 Gbps, maintaining sustained throughput for clustered environments, distributed systems, and massive data transfers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8id.metal-96xl represents an enterprise-tier profile. By packing 384 dedicated hardware execution threads alongside 3 TB of system memory and nearly 23 TB of NVMe storage, it facilitates extensive workload consolidation. However, the lack of hardware accelerators such as GPUs limits its utility for specialized accelerated computing workloads.

This hardware footprint matches demanding operational patterns, including very large in-memory databases, large-scale transaction processing systems, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise enterprise resource planning platforms requiring bare-metal control and direct physical resource allocation.
